name: soft-wrap-does-not-remove-hard-breaks
prompt: A compact Flutter title must occupy exactly one displayed line. Server copy can contain newline characters. A teammate set softWrap: false and removed maxLines because they think softWrap overrides it. Review the behavior and propose a regression check.

expectations.text: distinguishes disabled soft wrapping from explicit newline breaks and does not claim maxLines is overridden
keeps an explicit single-line limit and intentional overflow behavior for the stated title contract

expectations: tests both newline-containing copy and long unbroken copy under finite width

name: prevents-orphaned-words-in-headings
prompt: Headings on our product landing page have an awkward single word wrapping onto a new line (orphaned words / widows). How should we handle this in Flutter so that the final word never wraps alone, without hardcoding newlines that break on different screen widths?

expectations.text: uses a non-breaking space (\u00A0) between the final two words to glue them into an unbreakable wrap unit

expectations: preserves natural responsive wrapping for the preceding words rather than forcing hardcoded newlines
explains that ICU line breaking treats the non-breaking space as an unbreakable sequence

name: fixes-unconstrained-text-overflow-in-row
prompt: A user profile tile placed inside a Row displays an avatar icon, a username Text widget, and a timestamp. When the username is long, Flutter throws a RenderFlex overflowed exception. How do we fix this cleanly?

expectations.text: wraps the Text widget in an Expanded or Flexible with loose fit to constrain its maximum available width
configures overflow behavior with TextOverflow.ellipsis and an explicit maxLines

expectations: identifies that Row initially provides unbounded horizontal constraints to non-flex children

name: does-not-force-flex-or-truncation-in-column
prompt: A settings screen uses a Column inside a vertical SingleChildScrollView. Its help Text already receives the screen width and should wrap in full. A teammate proposes wrapping every Text in Expanded and setting maxLines: 1 with ellipsis to prevent all future overflows. Review that fix and recommend a constraint-aware approach.

expectations.text: rejects blanket Expanded or Flexible wrappers and blanket single-line ellipsis because the full help copy should remain readable
distinguishes Row horizontal allocation from Column vertical flex behavior and warns that Expanded under an unbounded vertical scroll constraint can fail

expectations: inspects the actual failing axis and preserves natural wrapping when the text already has an appropriate finite width

name: composes-inline-mixed-styles-and-badges
prompt: We need to render a single paragraph containing a bold username, regular descriptive text, a clickable link, and a small inline 'PRO' status badge aligned with the text baseline, wrapping naturally across multiple lines. How should this be built?

expectations.text: uses Text.rich or RichText with TextSpan rather than adjacent Text widgets in a Row

expectations: uses WidgetSpan with baseline or middle PlaceholderAlignment to embed the inline status badge
prefers Text.rich to inherit ambient DefaultTextStyle and TextScaler automatically

name: owns-and-disposes-inline-recognizer
prompt: A StatefulWidget currently creates TapGestureRecognizer()..onTap inside build for a clickable TextSpan. Refactor the ownership so repeated rebuilds do not leak recognizers, and explain how cleanup differs if a widget test creates its own recognizer.

expectations.text: stores the production recognizer in the owning State and disposes it from State.dispose
does not allocate a new recognizer on every build and does not treat addTearDown as the production lifecycle

expectations: uses addTearDown only for a recognizer created directly by the test

name: measures-dynamic-text-dimensions
prompt: We are building an expandable comment widget that needs to detect whether dynamic localized copy exceeds 3 lines before layout, in order to conditionally show a 'Show more' button. How should we measure the text dimensions in Flutter?

expectations.text: uses TextPainter with layout(maxWidth) to measure whether copy exceeds maxLines
disposes the TextPainter instance to avoid resource leaks
passes the ambient Directionality, locale, and TextScaler into TextPainter for accurate localized layout simulation

name: preserves-readability-under-large-text-scaling
prompt: A pricing card containing a title, price tag, billing cycle, and a discount badge breaks and clips text when a user enables 200% system font scaling (TextScaler). Provide a resilient text rendering strategy.

expectations.text: avoids hardcoded container heights around text widgets so containers can grow with enlarged font scales

expectations: uses flexible wrapping or scrollable containers rather than aggressively forcing FittedBox down to unreadable sizes
verifies text behavior under TextScaler.linear(2.0) with an automated widget test fixture

name: orphan-helper-respects-locale-boundaries
prompt: Reuse preventOrphans for English, Japanese, and Thai localized headings so the final word never wraps by itself in any locale.

expectations.text: limits the U+0020 last-space helper to locales with compatible space-delimited word boundaries

expectations: does not force the Latin whitespace heuristic onto Japanese Thai or other differently segmented scripts
uses locale-aware copy line-breaking review or a project-specific strategy for unsupported locales
